text: Acute presentation with coffee-ground emesis and melena for 3 days. Hemoglobin 7.2. Tachycardic at 115 bpm. Upper endoscopy shows bleeding duodenal ulcer. Clips applied.
Annual health maintenance visit. 55-year-old female. BP 118/72. BMI 23.8. All cancer screenings current. Labs unremarkable. Counseled on bone health.
Ventricular fibrillation cardiac arrest in ED waiting room. Immediate CPR and defibrillation. ROSC after 2 shocks. Post-cardiac arrest care initiated. Cooled to 33C.
Routine follow-up for GERD. Symptoms well controlled on PPI. No alarm symptoms. No need for repeat endoscopy. Continue omeprazole. Return in 6 months.
Acute posterior circulation stroke. Vertigo, diplopia, ataxia, dysarthria. MRI confirms acute cerebellar and brainstem infarcts. Basilar artery stenosis on CTA.
Sports medicine consultation for runner's knee. Advised on stretching protocol, ice application, and gradual return to activity. NSAIDs PRN. Follow up in 3 weeks.
Severe sepsis from cholangitis. Fever 40.2C, RUQ pain, jaundice (Charcot triad). Total bilirubin 12. Emergent ERCP for bile duct decompression arranged.
Routine pediatric dental visit for 6-year-old. No cavities. Sealants applied to first molars. Good brushing technique demonstrated. Return in 6 months.
Massive PE with hemodynamic collapse. sPESI high risk. RV dilation on CT. Troponin and BNP elevated. Catheter-directed thrombolysis via IR initiated.
Annual eye exam for contact lens wearer. Corneal health good. Vision stable. New contact lens prescription issued. Return in one year.
Necrotizing pancreatitis with infected necrosis. CT shows walled-off necrosis with gas. Septic. Started on meropenem. Interventional radiology drainage catheter planned.
Routine physical for 10-year-old. Growth on track. School performance satisfactory. No behavioral concerns. Age-appropriate anticipatory guidance provided.
Rhabdomyolysis with CK 85,000 from marathon in extreme heat. Dark brown urine. Creatinine rising. Aggressive IV hydration lactated Ringer's. Monitoring for compartment syndrome.
Pre-travel health consultation. Updated tetanus booster. Hepatitis A vaccine administered. Traveler's diarrhea self-treatment kit prescribed. Safe travel advice given.
Hemorrhagic stroke with intraventricular extension. GCS 6. External ventricular drain placed in OR. Neurocritical care admission. Poor prognostic signs discussed with family.
Follow-up for seasonal rhinitis. Fluticasone nasal spray effective. No sinusitis symptoms. Continue current management. Annual follow-up or PRN for flares.
Guillain-Barré syndrome with rapidly ascending paralysis. Areflexia. Respiratory function declining FVC 1.2L. Started IVIG. ICU admission for ventilatory monitoring.
Routine newborn hearing screening. Otoacoustic emissions test passed bilaterally. No risk factors for hearing loss. No follow-up needed at this time.
Aortic valve endocarditis with large vegetation and embolic stroke. Blood cultures positive for Streptococcus. TEE confirms 1.5cm vegetation. Cardiac surgery consulted.
Annual wellness exam for healthy 35-year-old male. No complaints. Physical exam unremarkable. Lipid panel within normal limits. Discussed exercise and nutrition.
Acute fulminant myocarditis. New-onset heart failure EF 10%. Cardiogenic shock. VA-ECMO cannulation performed. Endomyocardial biopsy obtained. Giant cell myocarditis suspected.
Routine postpartum visit 6 weeks after uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Incision healed. Breastfeeding well. Mood screening negative. Contraception plan discussed.
Tension pneumoperitoneum from perforated gastric ulcer. Rigid abdomen and septic shock. CT confirms free air. Emergent exploratory laparotomy for source control.
Physical therapy evaluation for frozen shoulder. Range of motion measured. Treatment plan established with progressive stretching and strengthening. Twice weekly sessions.
Unstable cervical spine fracture C2 with spinal cord injury. ASIA B. Halo vest application and neurosurgical spine consultation for potential operative fixation.
